_comment: Up to v0.9, zlint's `rules` block was an ALLOWLIST: naming ANY rule disabled every
rule not named, so a config listing only the rules you wanted off silently disabled
all the others and the tree reported '0 errors, 0 warnings' vacuously. v0.10.0 made
it an override layer (unnamed rules run at their defaults). This file still names
all seventeen, so what runs is a decision recorded here rather than a default that
arrives with a version bump, and the canary in scripts/check.py still has to fail.
OFF, deliberately -- each is a house convention rather than a latent bug. Counts
are zlint v0.10.0's on 2026-10-02; recount when one is cited:
suppressed-errors (45 hits), audited 2026-10-02. Two kinds. About half are
`catch unreachable` where the line above bounds the input or checks the room
(fmt into a fixed buffer, a frame after `available()`), or a test helper. The
rest are `catch {}`: best-effort cleanup (a GOAWAY before a close), a
`Thread.yield` in a spin, a best-effort madvise or affinity whose effect is
read back elsewhere, and the fuzzer discarding decode errors on purpose. Each
one not obvious from its own line says why. The audit found one that could
hang a connection (`sendInitialFrames` on a fresh one) and it now closes
instead. Turning this to `warn` would mean 45 permanent warnings nobody
reads, which is worse than an explicit decision recorded here.
unsafe-undefined (59 hits): `var x: T = undefined` immediately before the call
that fills it -- clock_gettime, read buffers, HPACK scratch. §6.3 forbids
allocation on the request path, so preallocated-then-filled is the house
pattern and it appears everywhere.
no-print (8 hits): bench/micro and bench/graphdiff print their own results and
usage, which is what a benchmark tool is for. The other six are the engine's
index log in src/core/collection.zig (`index: rebuild start ...`, behind
`log_rebuilds`, off in tests): the lines fullrun keeps in server-*.log and the
findings quote, written to stderr where the harness already reads them.
case-convention (8 hits, 7 in bench/isa/asm_probe.zig): `export fn sm_dot_f32`
and friends. §6.6.3 requires each kernel be a real symbol so objdump can find
it and docs/asm/ can be diffed; C-ABI exports are snake_case by convention and
Zig follows C for extern/export. Every one there is deliberate. The eighth is
a false positive: `engineDefault` in src/main.zig returns a value whose type
is computed, and zlint reads the computed type as the function returning one.
duplicate-case (6 hits since v0.10.0): it now flags switch arms with identical
bodies, not duplicate values, which Zig already rejects at compile time. Every
hit is a protobuf decoder skipping a field (`3 => try r.skip(...)` beside `4 =>`)
where each arm says why its field is skipped; merging them loses that.
allocator-first-param (14 hits): strawmANN threads the *subject* first --
`searchQuantized(coll, query, ..., alloc, out)` -- so a call site reads as the
thing being operated on followed by how. Moving the allocator first would read
worse at 14 sites to satisfy a convention the codebase does not hold.
no-return-try (7 hits): `return try x` in the decoders and h2. The `try` says
the line propagates an error, and it adds this frame to the error return
trace, which is what a decode failure is debugged from.
line-length (186 hits): `zig fmt` is the formatter of record and does not wrap.
Most hits are long expected strings in src/api/handlers.zig and e2e.zig, where
the whole expectation on one line is the clearest form of the test.
Everything else is ON. `unused-decls` in particular stays on because dead code is
how a tier ends up implemented, unit-tested and never wired into a run -- which is
what happened to T4 and to five of §8.6's seven metamorphic properties.
A clean run is therefore MEANINGFUL rather than vacuous: the canary test is to add
an unused decl and confirm zlint still fails.
